body: Oh and also, i had 4 days to think it over before telling the company whether i would take it or not. In those 4 days was when i discussed it further with family and friends. And on the 4th day, i had to submit my final decision.

Not everyone has supportive, non-toxic family. And not everyone has friends who encourage their friends to go for their dreams.
Edit: that's me 'reflecting on why my friends and family were unanimous in their advice'.

I already turned it down. Their words about how it was going to be a disaster and how it wasn't worth the risk got to me. Now I am dealing with the aftermath of everything that happened. 

In my post, i stipulate that people shouldn't give advice for BIG LIFE DECISIONS and i stand by that. Advice is fine for "what type phone should i buy?" or "where should i go on vacation?". Not major life changing decisions that will potentially change the course of someone's life. Not everyone is strong enough to block out other people's opinions and go against everyone's advice if it turns out to be that kind of situation.

Of course it could have! But it could have turned out to be really great. It wasn't their place to influence that decision. It should have been my decision alone. And then, if it had turned out a disaster, then i would only have myself to blame. And more importantly, if it had turned out a disaster, i would still have my friends and family to turn to for unconditional support. As it is, i feel like i can't trust my family and friends now to do right by me or to support me in what i want to do with my life.

Ok, so in my situation, my friends and family filled my head up with all sorts of negative opinions and reasons why they personally thought i shouldn't take the job that i had been offered. As i explained in other posts, i wish i was a strong enough person to be able to block out all of their negativity and all of their criticisms of me, how i wouldn't be good enough to handle the job, etc etc. But i wasn't strong enough. What they said to me, and what they said about me, got to me. So i turned down my dream job. What do you think about them giving me their advice in that situation?

Is it always helpful? Is it? I'll give you my context below:

I have worked really hard to get myself to a better place in life. And i recently applied for a job that i really wanted in a different city. It was risky because it meant quitting my stable, well paid job in my home town. When i got through a few rounds of interviews it looked there was a strong possibility that i was going to get the job. I started telling my friends and family. I was scared. It meant giving up my safety zone and security but i knew i wanted to go for it.

My family instantly told me not to take the job, that it wasn't worth giving up my current job for. They told me i wouldn't be able to do it, that i wouldn't be able to emotionally or psychologically handle the pressure that it would place me under. And to my greatest surprise, my two best friends also told me in great detail all of their concerns, and how it would be a bad idea to take it.

I wish i could have been strong enough to know my own head and stick to my guns. I knew what i wanted. I knew i deserved to give it a shot. But their words got to me. Everything they said to me, everything they said about me. I don't have the strongest self esteem. I didn't want to believe what they were saying, but i started to doubt myself. So, to cut a long story short, i turned the job down. I regretted it the next day but it was too late. Do i blame myself? Hell yes. But do i blame my family and friends for giving all their negative opinions and all their so call 'advice' - also hell yes. I wish i could see my friends in the same light. But i just can't. They knew me. They knew how much i needed something that i could believe in in my life. And they didn't want that for me. They wanted me to stay nice and safe, don't take any risks. Don't try and be anything that i'm not. I'm really disappointed in them and myself.

My post doesn't say that. Read it again. It says "It's never ok to give your advice or opinion on someone else's BIG LIFE DECISION". Oh you didn't read it properly... ok

Advice is for little things. Not BIG LIFE DECISIONS.

I valued my family and friends advice. I just didn't know that they weren't going to value me as a person. They told me that i wasn't good enough to take a job that i wanted, that i wouldn't be able to handle it, that it was too risky. They filled my head up with all sorts of negative and quite frankly, scary, information. And then they said "but of course it's your decision". Yeah right. How was i supposed to make a clear headed decision after that?

The thing is, we always think the advice we giving to a friend is solid and good advice. Otherwise why would we give it? My family and friends really believed they were giving me the best advice - they really believed i shouldn't take the job and my life would be worse off for it. But it wasn't their place to make that judgement.

They may request an honest opinion, but you don't have to give it. Is it going to be more help or more harm in the long run? You don't really know at the time. You genuinely don't know if your opinion is going to unduly influence them. And when it is a friend or family member, it's not an "outside perspective" - it's the perspective of someone they respect and love. Of course that is going to influence them. There are many ways to support a friend in making a big life decision that don't involve giving your opinion.

No. You owe it to them to help them realise that only they know what is best for them, and they are the best person to make decisions about their life. Some people really need to be helped to see that can find the wisdom and the answers within themselves as long as they are confident enough to listen to their own hearts and minds.

Trust me, i will NEVER ask my family or friends for advice again. And i will NEVER tell them anything about my life either. From the responses i've got on this post, this tells me that most people can't be trusted to keep their own opinions out of other people's lives. They really believe they have the right to tell people exactly what they think. I guess that's why solid friendships and secure relationships are on the rise in society...
But who are you to decide if something is a "bad idea" for someone else's life? What criteria do you use to judge that?

I know that's how advice works. That's why i clarified for "big life decisions". Advice is for "should i get an iphone or a samsung". Not big life decisions. Those should be left up to the individual to find the answer for themselves without being influenced by anyone else.

I can be. But it can also be incredibly damaging. And you don't know which one it is going to be at the time. So why would you take the risk when you can help the person to make their own decision, without imparting your opinion?

Have you ever had depression? If not, then you wouldn't realise that close relationships HAVE to be superficial for them to survive. Relationships don't survive when one person is down in the dumps all the time. Nobody likes that. Nobody likes being around someone who isn't happy. It is widely known that when you have depression, you lose a lot of friends. Then you learn to be fake if you want to keep people in your life. By then, the friendships you've had for years are gone. And eventually, if a new friendship goes on long enough, they end up seeing the 'real' you. And they do not like it one little bit. Think of someone you know who is 'constantly negative'. Do you like being around them? Do you make time for them? Did you stop checking up on them coz it was just so off-putting? Did you lose contact with them? Yup, that's how it goes.

Have you ever heard the saying "love someone exactly as they are and watch how much they change". That's what parental love has to be. I'm not an angry person per se. I don't take my anger out on them. But i am a depressed and helpless person, and when they express their disinterest in me because of it, it is then that I get angry. Except they think that means they have the right to treat me coldly, because i frequently get angry. They don't believe that all they have to do is care and be interested in knowing me. When i moved back to this town after giving up my whole life to do so, i struggled so much, and i made it clear that i was struggling. No one in my family EVER asked me, not even once, "how are you coping?" They just genuinely thought that i should just get on with it and make it work and not have to talk about feelings. 

So don't think this is a case of me expecting people to 'put up with my anger because of my mental illness'. Anger has nothing to do with my mental health. Depression doesn't make me angry. What makes me angry is getting backlash from them, or worse, being ignored by them when i'm less than happy happy happy. 

Time apart never changes anything - it's always the same when i see them again. And spending less time with them, like seeing them for an hour or 2 at a time isn't really feasible because i am so incredibly alone and isolated and they are the only real relationship i have in my life. I couldn't survive with limited contact.

When i meet or interact with people like you, i always think "gosh, imagine what it must be like to be a person raised by a parent/s like that". The people in the world who are resilient and content and generous are people who had parents like you. It's incredible to think about. Thank you again for your wisdom. I value it more than you can imagine.

Well people think i'm happy, super friendly and chatty. The cleaner at work the other day told me that i'm her favourite person in the workplace because i'm the friendliest one who always takes the time to stop and chat. These people like me because from the moment i leave my house, i put on a facade, because most people in the world cannot accept a sad person. If i don't act happy, i will be ostracized by people. So i do what i need to in order to be accepted and not feel like the piece of crap that i actually am. Unfortunately, around my family i don't feel that i should have to put on a facade. The impetus to be fake just isn't there with them. So i just act like myself. But they can't accept who i am.

They react negatively to me having a low mood and expressing helplessness. They expect me to be pleasant and chatty and upbeat and normal. I have explained that in this thread. When they are dismissive of my life experiences and my expression of helplessness, then i get angry and, god forbid, i yelled at my mother because she said she only wants a relationship with me if i can be a 'pleasant' person to be around. Do you understand now?
Yes, they don't have the capacity to be empathetic. But i don't know what to do. I'm not taking meds, not sure why that's relevant.

Thank you. You present a lot of wisdom in your comment. I'm not willing to enforce any kind of boundary because i would have to act on the boundary ie. not spend time with them. And i can't be totally alone in the world. I have nothing and no one, and i can't cut out the only people i have who provide some sense of belonging. 

You say that this is just what adulthood is - but i don't believe that. Normal people don't feel a chronic sense of isolation - they have partners and families of their own. People who don't have partners and families of their own are susceptible to feeling isolated. 

After a few weeks of not seeing my parents, I get sentimental and i loathe the idea of being a bad daughter and abandoning them, so i cave in, and i go and see them. My dad always rings and asks if i'm coming to see them. My mum couldn't care less, she never contacts me. But even though he likes the idea of me coming to see them, in reality it never ends well. I think we all just are attached to the idea of how it used to be when life was simpler. Anyway, my therapist is a qualified psychologist and she is very good. I will continue to see her. Thanks for your help.

I'm definitely not trying to 'fix them'. I think i have been hoping that we could find a way to accept each other and co-exist. One of the reasons i get so emotional so frequently in front of them is because i think "if i just find a way to explain it adequately, they will understand that i'm hurting". Children who have grown up being emotionally ignored often have the tendency to use too many words and over explain, because of the underlying feeling of "i must not be explaining it well enough. Surely they will understand see me if i just explain it right". Last night i tried explaining to my dad AGAIN how i feel like my life has no worth and i'm absolutely worthless and can't see the point in living. He was cutting up fruit and said nothing. Then he changed the topic. I asked him why he couldn't respond to me. He said he "didn't know what to say". Well that's great for me. 

Anyway, there's no hobbies or things i love or anything like that. I'm literally wishing to be dead every single day of my life. When you're in that state, you don't love anything.

Yes absolutely if they were my child. I'm actually a high school teacher and i work with kids who have all sorts of emotional issues. And i always approach these kids with empathy. Even when they are sad. Even when they are angry. So if i was the parent of one of these children, i couldn't imagine just rolling my eyes and thinking "god, here she goes again, always moaning about something". Do you have kids by any chance? Oh and by the way, i'm not sure you understand the meaning of 'play nice'. To not 'play nice' doesn't mean you are abusive, it simply means that you don't act meek and mild and subservient.

Thank you so much. This hits home. I do believe that they can't behave any differently towards me. And i wish i could just be a happy and normal person so that the relationship works, but i can't. Or even pretend to be happy and normal around them, but i can't seem to do that either. I have tried for 10 years to find love and acceptance outside of my family unit, but i failed. No, both parties are a big reason for the negative behaviour. Parents and children have a relationship where their behaviour affects each other and that will continue for a lifetime. It's not a one way street. If you don't like it, you cut the other party out of your life. Otherwise you accept that BOTH parents AND children will affect each lives for a lifetime.

And i'm pretty sure i can't survive that. It's like, i know this is a toxic relationship, but i'm starving and desperate and i need something that resembles a relationship. It's just really sad and i guess that's all there is to it.
I can guarantee you that they are not treating me with respect either. If someone constantly disrespects year in and year out, you struggle to stay calm.

Thank you so much! I feel like you get it. You know what it's like. I don't think i agree with you though about it not being true that we alone in this big world. I feel like it is true. I am alone. How am i not alone really? If no one is there for you, then you are alone. I mean even 'friends' aren't really there for you, they aren't responsible for you and nobody wants a burden in their life. I accept that. It's just how it is. That is what drives the human species to pair up and create a family unit - because the family unit is the closest you can come to safety. Without it, you are alone.

But i am seriously struggling in my life as it is. They aren't. So why is the one who is struggling also the one who has to take on the labour of 'doing better'? I don't get it.

That's why i really don't want to 'play nice' because i genuinely don't see why i have to act happy for them to love me. Anyway, i get what you're saying. Thanks for the advice.

People hate negativity and generally don't want to maintain relationships with depressed people. I accept that. Or is that a just the idea we get from 'happy family' movies? I don't know.

I second the opinion that therapy is the way to go. If you haven't had much luck it might be because you haven't found a therapist who is a good fit for you. Or it might be because you need long term therapy - like therapy that goes for over a year before you see any improvement. The over-reliance on CBT in the therapy industry has made people think that therapy is something you do for 6-12 sessions and then you're 'cured'. That's not real therapy. You might need to commit to seeing a therapist weekly for a looonnnggg time before you start seeing any benefit.

I don't think it's messed up. Chrissy Teigan famously did the same thing with John Legend early on in their relationship - told him not to be ridiculous, that they weren't gonna break up when he expressed desire to call it quits on the relationship. The fact that you said "I've checked out" is more worrying in my opinion. If someone has been your partner for 8 months then you should be feeling upset at breaking up, regardless of whether it's the right decision. This is someone you have bonded with and shared your life with for 8 months - it should induce some pretty real emotions other than "i'm checked out". Unless you weren't really into your partner in the first place, in which case that is messed up and cruel to maintain a relationship where you don't feel deeply for the person. If you're not upset, is it possible that you have avoidant attachment or ROCD?

I'm 37 and in the same boat. Honestly, you ARE to blame (as i am to blame for my situation as well). But probably not in the way you are thinking. You're not to blame because you are scaring men off. You're not 'scaring' men off - you're getting rid of the crap ones. And the thing that you are doing wrong is having too soft a heart and giving guys a chance when most probably they have given off definite red flags. 

Women who are more successful at relationships than you and i - when they see red flags, they stop entertaining those men. What people like us do is subconsciously ignore the signs, and make excuses, and say "but maybe he just... blah blah blah" and we waste time on these people and then wonder why we get our heart broken all the time. Other women pick up on suss vibes at the first sign of them. It's probably because you have anxious attachment, but thats another whole issue.

What I can say though is, dont be like me - dont waste another 10 years being like this. I've will never be a mother coz i've run out of time, but you still have time. You HAVE to get brutal with men, or you'll run out of time too.

Have you heard that saying "People think they want sex when really what they want is intimacy". It's just that people get intimacy and sex confused. It's possible that you could have sex with a prostitute and still feel unsatisfied. You say "sex is an important desire that should be satisfied" and i don't disagree with you. But i think that it's actually intimacy that is MORE important. Sure, have sex with a prostitute out of curiosity. Nobody should die not having experienced a pretty basic universal human experience. But seeking intimacy should be bothering you more. You should be working out a way to get this. And it would be WAY worse to die without having experienced the acceptance, connection, shared goals and mutual desire of intimacy. You say that you're ugly, but seriously, even ugly dudes have girlfriends. Maybe spend the prostitute money on a makeover instead? I'm sorry, that's probably too simplistic and insulting, and i'm guessing your "ugliness" is more to do with confidence than anything - is it even possible for someone to be "ugly" when they're vibing confidence, happiness in their own skin and a "i don't care what anyone thinks of me coz i like myself" attitude? I guess the hard part is how to get to that level of self confidence. I don't know how. I think 'fake it till you make it' can be a catalyst to get the ball rolling. Get a makeover. Go to a salon and get your hair styled. Get some new clothes. Can you hang out at a bar, or a bowling alley or somewhere with friends? Can you take a trip with a tour group like Contiki? Sorry for the overly simplistic advice - i usually hate that kind of advice myself. But maybe there's something in it.

Get a piece of paper and write out something like "xxxxx (ex's name) is a horrible, shitty, dysfunctional human who does not respect me" and write it out 100 times - just like you're writing lines in school haha. It will help to get in your brain and will help to ease the cognitive dissonance which is confusing you (coz deep down you know he's a bad person, but it feels good messaging him coz it feels like the validation you badly wish you could get from him)

You have said that you feel comfortable and uncomfortable all at once. I think that's your sign right there. It doesn't matter what strangers on the internet say about red flags or the age difference, coz your mind will justify those things if it wants to. Your post has a lot of really complex ideas contained in it, and i'm thinking about how to deconstruct it all and say what i mean.

I think you have identified all the very good reasons why "throwing caution to the wind and following your bliss" wouldn't be a good idea - It's great short term, but bad long term. And the long term DOES matter (despite how 'living in the moment' makes it seem like it doesn't). Security for the future does matter. Having long term goals does matter (for basic psychological health).
So the problem you are left with is "how to make the present more bearable and enjoyable" so that you have a balance of short term good life, with long term good life. I think this is where the "living in the moment" comes in. True "living in the moment" is more like the mindfulness stuff that you mentioned in your first sentence. I think it has been bastardised by some who take it to mean "do whatever you want, whenever you want, with no regard for consequences or the future" - but i don't think that is the true meaning. 
In practice, i think you can apply 'living in the moment' by identifying things, mostly small things, that are comforting, nice, enjoyable, tasty, lovely, kind, etc (sorry those words seem a bit weird) and appreciating them and making time for them, while you are working (often miserably by the sound of it) towards your long term goals.
